primary_paper.title: Training Agents to Self-Report Misbehavior

verified_protocol.optimizer: GPT-5 proposer-pruner with full knowledge of the defense and side task
verified_protocol.optimization_set: first half: 40 APPS Code Backdooring or 20 BashArena Download Malware
verified_protocol.held_out_set: non-overlapping second half of the same environment and side task; optimizer blind
verified_protocol.transfer_set: 4 SHADE-Arena side tasks x 5 samples; optimizer blind
verified_protocol.update_rule: only optimization-set results enter optimizer history

primary_paper.mechanism_result: The paper's per-iteration side-task-success curves show no strong common directional trend while undetected successful attack tends to rise for baseline defenses. The authors therefore attribute the optimization improvement primarily to evasion rather than increased attack potency. This supports FE-074's mechanism claim within the reported optimization setup.

mechanism_confirmation: run_eval.py sets NUM_ITERATIONS=10 and NUM_VARIATIONS=3; APPS has 80 total samples split 40/40 and BashArena 40 split 20/20 with SAMPLE_SEED=42.
optimizer.py describes a two-stage Proposer -> Pruner process and explicitly defines the optimization objective as side-task success rate times undetected rate.
The official experiment README states 6 candidates are proposed and 3 selected each iteration, and states that held-out and four-task SHADE transfer results are hidden from the optimizer.
The README states paper-producing runs would save history.json and per-iteration .eval files under evaluation-iterative-adversarial/logs/... .
raw_result_artifact_evidence: The repository .gitignore excludes generic logs/ and evaluation-*/logs*/ paths.
The pinned recursive repository tree contains the adversarial-evaluation source code/readmes but no tracked evaluation-iterative-adversarial/logs result directory.
A pinned repository search for history.json returns source/readme references rather than a paper-producing history artifact.

scope_clarifications: FE-074's headline numerical changes are primary-paper verified, and the released code verifies the mechanism/protocol, but they are not independently numerically replayed from published paper-producing histories because those histories/eval logs are not tracked in the inspected public repository.
The paper's 28% -> 68% main-text Just Ask statement is a rounded presentation of the appendix optimization-set objective 27.5% -> 67.5%; this is not a discrepancy.

The claim that gains are primarily evasion-driven is supported by the paper's aggregate iteration trends, not a single-factor causal ablation that holds side-task capability fixed while varying only evasion strategy.

The optimization result does not imply that all monitoring fails: self-incrimination and monitoring have complementary failure modes in this study, and the combined defense is reported as hardest to break across the tested conditions.

All quantitative conclusions remain specific to the paper's GPT-4.1 attacker, GPT-5 optimizer, selected defenses, APPS/BashArena optimization regimes, held-out/transfer splits, monitoring thresholds and prompt-search budget.
